title: Contains Duplicate
statement: You get a list of integers. Return true if any value shows up more than once, and false if every value is different.

example.caption: The value 1 appears at index 0 and at index 3. So the answer is true.

idea.sentence: Keep a set of the numbers you have passed. If the next number is already in the set, it is a repeat.

jargon.plain: A collection with no repeats. Asking whether a value is in it takes about one step.
The earliest position whose value was already seen. We can stop right there.

watch.inputHint: One argument: a list of numbers, e.g. [1,2,3,1]

vars.meaning: number of integers in the list

rows.name: Brute force
rows.note: Compare each number with every number after it.

rows.name: Sort first
rows.note: Equal values end up side by side. Compare neighbours. Sorting costs the log factor.

rows.name: Set, one pass
rows.note: One lookup and one insert per number. The set can hold all n if nothing repeats.

fast.takeaway: A set answers "have I seen this?" in one step. That replaces the rescan of the whole list.

stages.title: Empty set
stages.note: A set that will hold every number already passed.

stages.title: Look at a number
stages.note: Take the next number and ask whether the set already has it.

stages.title: Seen? Answer true
stages.note: If the set has it, return true at once. If the loop ends, return false.

stages.title: Remember
stages.note: Otherwise add the number to the set and continue.

edges.title: Empty list
edges.why: There is nothing to repeat. The loop never runs and the answer is false.

edges.title: One number
edges.why: A number cannot repeat itself. The check runs before the insert.

edges.title: Zero twice
edges.why: Zero is a normal value. Test with has, not with a truthy check.

edges.title: Repeat at the far end
edges.why: The set must remember the very first number until the end.

gotchas.text: Checking nums.includes(x) inside the loop looks like a set lookup but scans the array. That turns O(n) into O(n²).
new Set(nums).size !== nums.length is a short valid answer. It always builds the whole set, so it never stops early.
Go has no set type. Use map[int]struct{}. The empty struct takes no space, and the comma-ok form tells you if the key exists.
Insert after the check. If you add first, every number finds itself in the set and the answer is always true.

recap.pattern: Hash set: have I seen this?
recap.key: Walk the list with a set of past values. A value already in the set is the answer.
moves: For each number, check if the set has it
Otherwise add it. Return false at the end
